description: Explains alcohol and carbonyl protection, reagent incompatibility, orthogonal deprotection and route-level tradeoffs, including when a protecting group is unnecessary.

related_resources.reason: Silyl ethers, nucleophile incompatibilities and protection cycles.
Acetal stability under many neutral/basic conditions and acid hydrolysis.
Retrosynthetic disconnection and testing candidate routes forward.

historical_claims.anchor: an ordinary Grignard reagent is strongly basic and is incompatible with an unprotected alcohol that can donate a proton.
Acetals are relatively stable under many neutral and basic conditions, but they can be hydrolyzed under aqueous acidic conditions
historical_claims.source_locator: Differential acetal stability and carbonyl regeneration.

historical_claims.anchor: Do we necessarily need to protect the aldehyde before a Suzuki reaction? No.
historical_claims.source_locator: Protection is chosen on demonstrated incompatibility, not routine assumption.

authorship.scope: Original organic synthesis and selectivity lecture, scientific companion and source-linked catalog metadata.

background: Introductory organic molecular structure, carbonyls, bonding and reaction mechanisms. All additional specialist ideas are introduced in the narration.
